subject: SOW edits / capacity add & rollback language — next steps
messages:
From: Andrew Chu <andrew.chu@medisight.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed SOW edits: add throughput tier and rollback clause

Hi Evelyn / Jordan,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call last week. We reviewed the draft SOW internally and have two immediate asks before procurement will sign: 1) add an additional reserved throughput tier ("Tier C" +2 GPUs equivalent) for our pilot expansion, and 2) include an explicit rollback/termination transition clause that protects our customer-facing features during deprovisioning (we need 30 days of degraded throughput with guaranteed cache pre-warm).

Commercially, we expect the Tier C add to be prorated from the effective date and prefer a short-term pilot rate (20% discount for first 90 days). Our LegalOps team also flagged data-residency language around KV cache persistence — they asked us to loop in Redwood legal for a brief review.

Attached is the SOW v2 with highlighting (Medisight_SOW_v2.docx). Can you confirm what you need from our side to get a coordinated legal + ops redline and an estimated timeline? We're targeting a September 6 cutover pending approvals.

Appreciate it —
Andrew
Andrew Chu
Head of Platform Integrations
Medisight

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Draft change order + commercial bullets (for Medisight)

Eve / Markus — following up on Andrew's ask (see quoted). I've put together a short draft change order and captured the commercial positions we should offer. Attachment: ChangeOrder_Draft.pdf

On Mon, Aug 30, 2027 at 9:12 AM Andrew Chu <andrew.chu@medisight.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the quick onboarding call last week. We reviewed the draft SOW internally and have two immediate asks before procurement will sign: 1) add an additional reserved throughput tier ("Tier C" +2 GPUs equivalent) for our pilot expansion, and 2) include an explicit rollback/termination transition clause that protects our customer-facing features during deprovisioning (we need 30 days of degraded throughput with guaranteed cache pre-warm).
> 
> Commercially, we expect the Tier C add to be prorated from the effective date and prefer a short-term pilot rate (20% discount for first 90 days).

Summary of proposed commercial language (draft):
- Effective date: day change order executes (DocuSign). Tier C prorated to calendar day of execution.
- Pilot discount: 20% off list for first 90 days for Tier C only; revert to standard tier pricing thereafter.
- Billing: monthly invoice with prorated first invoice.
- SLA & rollback: temporary SLA exception during pilot initiation (48 hours for scaled up capacity warm-up), formal rollback transition: 30-day notice by either party with staged throughput reductions (full description in Ops section).
- Acceptance: Ops runbook sign-off by Medisight SRE within 5 business days of capacity provisioning.

Asking legal to weigh in on the rollback wording and KV cache persistence obligations. If legal is comfortable with the staged-throughput description above, I'll send the change order to Andrew for an initial commercial ok and route to DocuSign.

-Jordan
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Draft change order + commercial bullets (for Medisight)

Jordan / Eve — quick legal feedback below. I'm also attaching a redline that highlights the specific rollback language I'm changing (SOW_Redline_Markus_comments.docx).

Notes:
- The phrase "staged throughput reductions" is too vague and creates operational ambiguity. Suggest replacing with a defined schedule: "Upon 30-day notice, Redwood will reduce provisioned throughput in three equal stages (Day 0-10, Day 11-20, Day 21-30) and will coordinate a cache pre-warm window of up to 48 hours prior to each stage."
- KV cache persistence: we cannot guarantee long-term persistence beyond the provisioning term unless Medisight accepts specific storage & egress terms. Suggest an optional exhibit that defines retention windows and egress procedures.
- Pilot discount: agree commercially but need to add a clause that disallows retro-active credit beyond 60 days to avoid long-tail accounting issues.
- Data residency: if they require pre-seeded cache copies in a different region, we need CISO approval; mark this as a gating item in the change order.

If Eve/Jordan want, I can convert my inline edits into a tracked-change SOW redline and circulate to Andrew. We should also list the required internal signoffs (Legal, Finance, CISO if region cross-over) before routing for signatures.

-Markus
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
